physics_plausibility_gate.broken_generator_mechanism: The unpatched upstream ScatteringGenerator at b73ea2a had the unit-weight sampling bug. When CSFile failed to load (missing dedx/sigma in cwd or wrong path), it fell back to a uniform distribution over [0,180] degrees instead of the physics-motivated p(theta) = sigma(theta) * sin(theta) / Z. This inflated the scattering-angle distribution toward large angles, dramatically increasing the rate of events reaching the B-arm trigger layer. The corrected generator enforces fail-closed behavior (FATAL on CSFile load failure) and samples from the measured cross-section support, producing physically realistic angular distributions.
physics_plausibility_gate.energy_budget_sanity: The corrected MC shows Enter B rate reduced from 23.710% to 0.710% of beam events. For a 190 MeV deuteron beam on a 2.3 mm CD2 target, scattering angles > ~30 degrees (required to reach the B arm) correspond to large momentum transfers. The differential cross-section falls sharply with angle — the Ermisch et al. data shows sigma(26 deg) ~= 4.6 mb/sr but sigma(170 deg) ~= 0.01 mb/sr. The 33x reduction in Enter B is consistent with sampling from the physically-measured cross-section rather than a uniform distribution. This is a physics-plausibility check: the corrected generator produces angular yields that follow the known physics of p-d elastic scattering.
physics_plausibility_gate.external_anchor: The Ermisch et al. PRC 71 064004 (2005) Table VI measurements are the community standard for 190 MeV p-d elastic scattering. Our corrected generator uses this table directly (sigma_pd_cm_190.txt). The historical uniform-fallback generator did not use this physics input. The corrected baseline is therefore anchored to experimental data.

size_delta_explained.explanation: The 47% size reduction (677 MB -> 356 MB) at identical event count is explained by the -97% reduction in tracking volume. The unpatched uniform-fallback generator produced 33x more B-arm hits, which in turn produced more secondary tracks and larger TTree branch sizes. The corrected generator's realistic angular distribution results in fewer stored hits per event, reducing the compressed file size. This is a secondary validation that the physics correction is working as intended.
size_delta_explained.correlation: Size delta correlates with Enter B delta: -97.01% Enter B -> -47% file size. Both are consequences of the corrected angular sampling.

wall_time_explained.expected_vs_observed: The '6-8h' estimate was an order-of-magnitude overestimate. The 1M run completed in under 2 minutes. This is consistent with the -97% tracking reduction: fewer hits means less TTree I/O and faster event processing.
wall_time_explained.correlation: Wall time reduction correlates with Enter B delta and size delta: fewer hits -> smaller TTrees -> faster I/O -> shorter runtime.

baseline_delta.methodology: scripts/phase1b_delta_table.py, which imports process_mc_file from scripts/trigger_baseline_characterization.py (the ORIGINAL characterization methodology — no reimplementation). Recomputed from BOTH ROOT files in SLURM job 3506920 after sha256 verification; receipts at research/trigger_migration_study/phase1b_baseline_{hist,authorising}_1M.json. Sanity gate passed exactly: hist enter_B 237,098 / auth 7,100; hist sample_I 64,762 / auth 554. The divergent counts published in an earlier draft (88,791 / 4,524 / 88,738 / 4,519, from an inline reimplementation) are RETRACTED.
baseline_delta.error_convention: Binomial sqrt(p(1-p)/n) on the ACTUAL denominator of each quantity: event rates n = 1,000,000 primary events; per-species eps_HRD n = species enter_B count; sample_I purity n = deuteron+proton sample_I count. Delta errors combine the two independent sides in quadrature. An earlier draft propagated errors on copy-pasted denominators (hist side used the AUTHORISING species counts 1,487 / 5,598 / 554; auth deuteron used the sample_I count 550 instead of enter_B 1,487) — those error columns were wrong and are corrected here.
baseline_delta.interpretation: The corrected ScatteringGenerator (physics-motivated cross-section sampling) reduces the HRD proxy rate by two orders of magnitude: Enter B 23.710% -> 0.710% (33x reduction, -97.01%), Sample I 6.476% -> 0.055%. Deuteron coincidence efficiency among B-arm deuterons drops 45.644% -> 36.987% (-8.66 ± 1.26 pp, 6.9 sigma): the fix changes not only how many events reach the B arm but the time/geometry structure of those that do. Proton eps_HRD drops 0.388% -> 0.071%. Deuteron purity of Sample I is statistically unchanged (99.423% -> 99.278%, delta -0.15 ± 0.36 pp): the surviving coincidence sample is still overwhelmingly deuteronic. Recorded as a finding in research/trigger_migration_study/PHASE1B_AUTHORISING_MC_FINDINGS.md; the table is regenerable via scripts/phase1b_delta_table.py.
